questions.text: What UART shell command, framing, and response protocol should access the register map?
questions.default: Use a simple documented 8N1 UART shell with 32-bit aligned register reads and writes at the listed offsets.
questions.reason: The request names a standard test shell and baud but does not define an existing protocol; this default makes register access implementable and scriptable.
questions.answer: Use a simple documented 8N1 UART shell with 32-bit aligned register reads and writes at the listed offsets.

questions.text: What exact debounce interval should each push-button use?
questions.default: Use 1000000 cycles of the 100 MHz clock, approximately 10 ms.
questions.reason: The request requires bounce immunity but gives no interval; 10 ms is a conventional compromise for mechanical switches.

questions.text: Should brightness value 255 mean exactly full-on or 255/256 duty?
questions.default: Use 256 PWM phases and a 255/256 duty for value 255, with zero fully off.
questions.reason: This follows a straightforward 8-bit compare implementation and avoids introducing an unspecified saturation special case.
questions.answer: Brightness value 255 means 255/256 duty, not exactly full-on; zero is fully off.
questions.evidence: - DUTY_EFF = 0 is fully off; 255 is on 255/256 of the time. Brightness is linear in DUTY_EFF (no gamma).

questions.text: Which control register bit selects the switches and which disables the display?
questions.default: CONTROL bit 0 selects SW[7:0] brightness and bit 1 disables the display.
questions.reason: No bit assignments are stated; adjacent low bits provide a simple stable register convention.
questions.answer: CTRL bit 0 selects SW[7:0] for brightness when set to 1. CTRL bit 1 is DISPLAY_EN, so setting it to 0 disables the display.
questions.evidence: - {offset: 0x02, name: CTRL,    access: RW, reset: 0x2,    bits: "[0] DUTY_SRC (1 = switches SW[7:0]); [1] DISPLAY_EN; [31:2] read 0"}

questions.text: How should brightness be represented on the two display digits when switch brightness is selected?
questions.default: Display the effective brightness value, whether sourced from the UART register or switches.
questions.reason: The text says the display shows the current brightness setting without specifying source precedence; showing the value actually driving PWM is the clearest behavior.
questions.answer: Display the effective brightness value in hexadecimal; when switch brightness is selected, this is the switch-sourced value.
questions.evidence: Digits 6 and 7 show DUTY_EFF[3:0] and DUTY_EFF[7:4] in hex.

questions.text: How should the design ID be encoded in the readable register?
questions.default: Return 0x54314443, corresponding to ASCII T1DC in most-significant-byte-first order.
questions.reason: The identifier text is specified but its binary encoding and byte order are not.
questions.answer: Return 0x54314443, corresponding to ASCII T1DC in most-significant-byte-first order.

questions.text: Should button press counts include the centre clear button, and what is their width?
questions.default: Maintain separate wrapping 32-bit counts for up, down, and centre presses, cleared by CPU reset.
questions.reason: The request asks how many times each button has been pressed without defining count width or reset behavior; counting all three user buttons with practical wide counters is unambiguous to test.
questions.answer: Yes. PRESSES includes separate counts for up, down, and clear; each count is 8 bits and wraps at 256. The register resets to 0, not to separate 32-bit counters.
questions.evidence: - {offset: 0x04, name: PRESSES, access: RO, reset: 0,      bits: "[7:0] up presses, [15:8] down, [23:16] clear; each wraps at 256"}

questions.text: What should happen if UART writes to the counter on the same cycle as a button event?
questions.default: Give the UART write priority over the button-derived counter update.
questions.reason: The request does not specify arbitration; prioritizing explicit software writes makes test-script results deterministic.
questions.answer: The UART write to COUNT wins; the button press still counts in PRESSES.
questions.evidence: A shell write to COUNT on the same clock as a press wins; the press still counts in PRESSES.

questions.text: What display scan rate and brightness reset value should be used?
questions.default: Scan each digit every 100000 clock cycles and reset UART brightness to 255.
questions.reason: Neither is specified; approximately 250 Hz full-frame refresh avoids visible flicker, and maximum default brightness makes the board visibly testable.
questions.answer: Scan each digit every 100000 clock cycles and reset UART brightness to 255.
